subject: Oceanography
title: Eutrophication
description: A micro-lesson that makes Eutrophication usable.

hook.text: Too many nutrients can be as deadly as too few—excess fertilizer turns coastal waters into graveyards.

buildup.text: Agricultural runoff floods coastal waters with nitrogen and phosphorus from farms.

discovery.text: This overload fuels algal blooms so dense they block sunlight and deplete oxygen when they decompose.

twist.text: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) produce toxins that kill fish, poison shellfish, and sicken humans.

climax.text: Eutrophication costs the US alone over $2 billion per year in lost fisheries and tourism.

punchline.text: Feeding the ocean too much fertilizer kills it.
